status: A design proposal on synthetic fixtures (11 November 2026), in no release. PROPOSED marks the design's own choices for review; the rest follows the owner's confirmed rules. Nothing here activates gameplay.

base.owner: docs/design/owner-decisions.md, 11 November 2026: the Food Supply Task's confirmed highlights
base.note: At this commit no Task, Food or Supply Room rule exists under rules/: the owner's 11 November highlights are the only rule source for this Task. Backend versions any adoption.

rules.rule: Initial food stock: five packages. Each successful supply delivery adds five packages.
rules.design: FOOD.initial 5, FOOD.perDelivery 5; the delivered card and the return toast say +5 packages.

rules.rule: The food warning appears when one package remains.
rules.design: FOOD.warnAt 1: the room banner "Food low: 1 package left" (PROPOSED: on every phone).

rules.rule: Each player consumes one dose at their Eating step. Not eating transfers them to Hospital under the existing Hospital rules.
rules.design: Not designed here (ship life shows the eating visits); see the open items.

rules.rule: A volunteer selects a Partner. Tasks happen outside ordinary turns; Task travel is separate from normal movement.
rules.design: Tasks sheet outside the turn order, then Choose your Partner; both travel to the Supply Room and back without a move.

rules.rule: Each player may initiate one Task total per match across Food and Engine. Partner participation can repeat without spending that initiation.
rules.design: The Tasks sheet says so; the server spends the Volunteer's initiation (when, see the open items).

rules.rule: One participant controls vertical movement; the other controls horizontal movement.
rules.design: The Hoist: Raise and Lower. The Boom: Left and Right. Two buttons each, nothing else.

rules.rule: Both can betray their partner using movement of the same controller: dropping the crate onto the other player, or driving a moving panel into them.
rules.design: The Hoist's Lower over the pulpit drops the crate on the Boom operator; the Boom's Left at the cab's door drives the gantry's bumper plate into the Hoist's cab.

rules.rule: There is no separate attack button, special trigger, confirmation or armed mode.
rules.design: The attack is the same button's ordinary press. The button is striped and says what it will do; nothing asks to confirm.

rules.rule: There is no escape opportunity. An unblocked attack is lethal and does not send its victim to Hospital. Protection applies.
rules.design: An attack resolves on the press, at once; the victim has nothing to press. KILLED is final (Eliminated); Protection gives STOPPED.

rules.rule: Each player has one attack opportunity. Its reset scope across repeated Task participation remains unspecified; do not silently choose it.
rules.design: The server passes each participant's opportunity into the Task and the design never resets it or shows it. The owner has since decided the scope: one per match, and a blocked attack uses it up (below).

rules.rule: After a partner dies, the survivor can complete the delivery alone if the crate is in the correct position. Otherwise the Task is lost.
rules.design: The correct position is the cradle (docked). A death with the crate docked: the survivor's key alone sends it. Otherwise: lost.

rules.rule: A participant disconnect cancels the Task.
rules.design: Cancelled after the grace (PROPOSED 8 s, see conflict 1). Nothing delivered; both return.

rules.rule: Other players do not see the Task space on their phones. This does not automatically authorize public killer attribution or Protection disclosure.
rules.design: Only the two participants' phones draw the Supply Room. No phone ever shows a killer, an attack kind or Protection to anyone else (see the visibility).

rules.rule: The ordinary return flow restores participants to their previous positions, accounting for death and cancellation.
rules.design: Each returns to the place they left; a dead participant is shown Eliminated there, as the board draws any death.

rules.rule: A short, understandable cooperative activity; low puzzle difficulty; coordination and trust are the challenge; both contribute without talking.
rules.design: Nine presses and two keys; the next press glows on the right phone; every risk is visible to both.

rules.rule: Other players can check on the board who is not here, so they can understand who went on the Task.
rules.design: While the Task runs, the two participants' places are empty on every board. A banner says that two players are away on the Food Supply Task, without names: the board shows who.

rules.rule: One attack opportunity per match, not one per Task.
rules.design: The server holds each player's attack for the whole match and passes it into every Task they join; once used, it is gone for the rest of the match.

rules.rule: A blocked attack uses up the opportunity.
rules.design: A STOPPED attack spends it as a kill would: the attacker cannot try again, in this Task or a later one.

rules.rule: Near each other, a small movement by both can kill one of them by mistake (a chance).
rules.design: Two zones: the crate over or beside the Boom operator's head, and the gantry at the cab's door. When both move within half a second there, the jolt kills the one in danger by chance (PROPOSED: 1 in 4); otherwise it is a close call (WHOA!). An accident is no one's attack: it uses no attack opportunity. PROPOSED: a Protected participant only ever has a close call.

rules.rule: The Partner can decline.
rules.design: The Partner request has Decline and Join. After a decline the Volunteer asks someone else or closes. PROPOSED: 15 s to answer, and no answer is a decline; the Volunteer's Task is used only when a Partner joins.

controls.press: One press, one step. Holding repeats every 300 ms (PROPOSED), the server's own interval: a press inside it is refused (too-soon). No drag, swipe or gesture; two big buttons for the participant's own axis only.
controls.deliberate: PROPOSED: attacks are deliberate. A hold's repeat stops at a warning, and an attack needs a fresh press on a button that showed it (TASK_MOVE shown and repeat). Not a confirmation or an armed mode: one press of the same button acts. A press that is not an attack still moves, or jerks, the machine, and moving together near someone can cause an accident (the owner's decision; see accidents).
controls.next: The press the cooperative route asks for next glows (amber ring), on both phones for their own button.
controls.keyboard: Arrow keys on the participant's own axis; the others do nothing.
controls.accessibility: Each button's accessible name says its warning ("Lower. Warning: drops it on Cleo."). The view is an image with a text equivalent (where the crate and the gantry are, and whether a warning shows). The hint is a polite live region. Large text: the controls keep their places (Raise above Lower, Left beside Right) and grow; the view gives way; cards scroll.

command.name: TASK_MOVE (a proposal for the shared contract; Integration owns packages/contracts/)

fields.about: 'up' | 'down' (the Hoist) or 'left' | 'right' (the Boom). The key presses are the same buttons: the Hoist's up, the Boom's right at the end stop, when docked.

PROPOSED: whether the pressed button showed the attack warning when pressed. A press that would attack with shown = false is not an attack: refused (stale), or, with the partner moving at the same moment, a jerk (JERKED) toward an accident.
PROPOSED: whether the press is a hold's repeat. A repeat never attacks (refused: repeat, or a jerk as above); a fresh press on the warning does.
The accident roll is the server's own random number for the press; the phone never sends or sees it.

command.answer: The new revision of the Task state with the events, to both participants; REFUSED to the presser only.

events.about: Who asks, and the time to answer.
Declined or no answer. The Volunteer asks someone else or closes.
Joined: the roles, then the briefing. Every board now shows the two places empty.

ask.visibility: PROPOSED: private to the two. Other players learn nothing until the Task starts, and then only that two players are away (the board shows who).

accidents.decision: The owner, 11 November 2026: "if Player A and B position and the result near each other and there is a small movement in both parts there is chance they kill each other by mistake".

boom.about: The crate over or beside the Boom operator's head: moving together, the swinging crate can hit them

cab.about: The gantry at the cab's door: moving together, it can lurch into the cab

accidents.rule: A jolt: both participants move the machine (a move, or a jerk) within the window, and the machine is in a zone before or after the second move. The server rolls: below the chance, an accident kills the zone's victim (unless Protected: then a close call); otherwise a close call. No attack opportunity is used. Bumps, keys and refusals are not movement.

food.eating: Each player eats one package at their Eating step; not eating sends them to the Hospital under the existing Hospital rules (confirmed). The Eating step's place in the round and the order of eating are not designed here (see the open items).

motion.cards: After a kill, the phones hold the outcome card until the impact cue has played, so both participants see the cause before the card covers the view.

events.fields: by, dir, from { crate, carriage }, to { crate, carriage }
events.about: One step: the crate on the hook, or the gantry with it.

events.fields: by, dir, why (rib | pulpit | lift | deck | rail | wall | stop | in-intake | cradle | key-turned)
events.about: Blocked: a clunk, nothing moves. The presser's hint says why.
The crate entered the cradle: the jaws shut. The correct position.
A key turned (the Hoist's Raise or the Boom's Right at the end stop, docked).
The Boom drove away from the end stop: its key turned back.
An attack press that did not kill: Protection, or no attack opportunity left. Identical either way.

events.fields: kind (drop | ram | swing | lurch), by (an attack only), accident (an accident only), victim, docked
events.about: An unblocked attack, or an accident: lethal, no escape, not the Hospital.
A press that would attack, made on an older picture or as a hold's repeat, while the partner is moving: not an attack; it counts toward a jolt.
A jolt that did not kill: a close call (WHOA!). The same for a lucky roll and for a Protected participant.
The server lost a participant's connection; the Task goes on.
Back within the grace: nothing paused.
Every living participant's key is turned: the lift goes up.
Delivered, lost or cancelled. The outcome card shows, then the return.

events.fields: seat, dir, why (briefing | too-soon | down | ended | not-your-axis | stale | repeat | not-a-participant)
events.about: The press did nothing; only the presser is told, and the phone shows the current state.

projection.about: Their own control: the Hoist (vertical) or the Boom (horizontal).
{ dir, label, key, hazard, enabled, next }: the two buttons. key: the button turns a key now. hazard: this press would attack. next: the cooperative route asks for it.
'crate-over-partner' | 'crate-over-you' | 'bumper-at-partner-cab' | 'bumper-at-your-cab': both participants see each position one press from an attack.
The cradle and the keys; needed counts the living participants.
The Task's time left; the briefing's countdown.
Attack opportunity, Protection, the other participant's refusals, and why a STOPPED happened: no phone can show them.

visibility.participants: Both see the whole Supply Room and its shared machine, every move and bump, both warnings, both keys, the time, and each other's alive or offline state. Both see a STOPPED alike, with no reason. Neither ever sees an attack opportunity, Protection, or the other's refused presses.
visibility.others: Never the Supply Room. The board shows who is away: the two participants' places are empty, so anyone can tell who went (the owner, 11 November 2026). A banner says only that two players are away on the Food Supply Task. PROPOSED: the result as the food stock shows it, delivered (+5) or nothing delivered; not how it went.
visibility.ask: PROPOSED: a Partner request and its answer are private to the two players: no one else learns who was asked, or that someone declined.
visibility.death: A participant killed on the Task is Eliminated at their previous position on the return, as any death is shown. No phone says who killed them, how, or that a Task killed them; the two participants already know.
visibility.protection: Never shown. A blocked attack is the same STOPPED as an attack by a participant with no opportunity left (see conflict 3). An accident never shows a STOPPED: a Protected participant has only a close call, exactly like a lucky roll.
visibility.accidents: Both participants see an accident or a close call as it happens (WHAM!, CRASH!, WHOA!), and the victim's card says it was an accident. Everyone else sees only the death, as any death: no cause, so a survivor can always say it was an accident.
visibility.foodStock: PROPOSED public: the count (the ship-life food capsules show it) and the warning at one package.
visibility.server: Only the server holds attack opportunities, Protection, and the reason for a STOPPED.

flow: A Volunteer opens Tasks (outside the turn order) and chooses Food Supply: one Task initiation per match across Food and Engine.
The Volunteer asks a Partner (PROPOSED eligibility: a living player outside the Hospital and the Jail, not already on a Task). Joining as a Partner never spends the Partner's own initiation.

The Partner can join or decline (the owner, 11 November 2026). PROPOSED: 15 s to answer, and no answer is a decline. After a decline the Volunteer asks someone else or closes; the Volunteer's initiation is used only when a Partner joins (PROPOSED). The request and its answer are private to the two (PROPOSED).

The server assigns the controls (PROPOSED: at random) and starts the Task: both travel to the Supply Room, separate from normal movement. Every board shows their two places empty, so anyone can see who went (the owner, 11 November 2026).
Briefing (4 s PROPOSED): who runs which control, the route, the warning stripes. The controls do nothing yet.
Running (45 s PROPOSED): presses, the shared machine, the warnings, the keys.
Ended: the outcome card (2.5 s PROPOSED), then the ordinary return flow restores each participant to their previous position, the dead as Eliminated where they were.

Lower while the crate hangs over the Boom operator
Drive the gantry into the Hoist operator's cab
The ram after docking: the crate stays clamped, and the survivor sends it alone
The Boom operator is Protected: the safety catch stops the crate
The Hoist operator is Protected: the cab's spring buffer stops the gantry
Both move at once while the crate hangs beside the Boom operator: the jolt swings it into them
proposed: A 1 in 4 chance when both move within half a second near someone

acceptance.about: The same jolt beside the Boom operator, and this time the crate only swings close
proposed: A 1 in 4 chance when both move within half a second near someone

acceptance.about: The crate never reaches the cradle before the deadline
A participant is out of contact longer than the grace
proposed: An 8-second grace before a disconnect cancels

acceptance.about: A press during the briefing does nothing.
A second press within the interval is refused; holding a button repeats at the interval.
A participant cannot press the other axis: the Hoist has no Left.
While the crate sits in the intake hatch, driving the gantry is a bump.
The crate crosses the rib only at the top row.
Lowering from the top row elsewhere is free; below the top row the crate cannot enter the pulpit's column from the side.
A Hoist who used the one attack of the match in an earlier Task lowers over the Boom: STOPPED, exactly as Protection would show.
A Protected Boom: the drop is stopped, and again on a second try: the first block used up the Hoist's one attack.
The Boom's key turns only at the end stop with the crate docked; driving away releases it.
Docked, the Hoist cannot lower further: a bump, and no drop is possible.
Out of contact for less than the grace: the Task never paused, and it goes on.
An attack that lands while the partner is out of contact stands: the Task ends lost, not cancelled.
Docked; the Hoist drops out of contact and the Boom rams the cab. The death stands, the dead Hoist's connection no longer matters, and the Boom sends alone.
A killed participant's presses do nothing.

Attacks are deliberate. Cleo drives the crate back over Cleo's own head just as Hana's Lower, pressed on the old picture, arrives: not an attack, only a jerk of the winch; with both moving at once it is a jolt, here a close call. A fresh Lower on the warning then drops it.
The same race with an unlucky roll: the jerk and the drive together swing the crate into Cleo. An accident: Hana's attack is not used.
The gantry at the cab's door and both moving at once: an unlucky roll lurches it into the cab. An accident: the Hoist is killed and the Task is lost.
The Boom is Protected and the roll is unlucky: still only a close call. No STOPPED, so an accident shows nothing about Protection.
The same crossing, but Hana waits until Cleo has stopped: no jolt, whatever the roll.
Both press at once at the cab's door, but Hana's Raise only bumps the rail: nothing moved, so no jolt.
PROPOSED deliberate attacks only. A held Raise or Lower repeats, but a repeat never carries into an attack: it stops at the warning, and only a fresh press attacks.
A participant out of contact for the whole grace: the Task is cancelled; both are alive and return.

conflicts.conflict: If a disconnect cancelled the Task at once, a player could escape an attack by dropping their connection (switching off the network), which "no escape" forbids, and a network blip would wipe out a Task.
conflicts.solution: The server judges a disconnect only after a grace (PROPOSED 8 s) in which the Task runs on: an attack pressed in the grace resolves, and a death that resolved before the cancellation stands (a dead participant's connection no longer matters). Back in time, nothing paused. Out longer, the Task is cancelled and both return.
conflicts.residual: A participant can still end a Task they dislike by staying offline. Whether a deliberate disconnect should cost anything is the owner's call (open item).

conflicts.conflict: The drop puts the crate onto the Boom operator, out of the cradle, so a Hoist who drops can never complete alone. Only the Boom's ram, after docking, can kill and still deliver. The rules make the two betrayals unequal.
conflicts.solution: Inside the rules: the server assigns the controls at random (PROPOSED), so neither player chooses the stronger seat; both phones show both risks equally; the two-key send makes docking a visible standoff (the Hoist's key turned and waiting is the moment to watch the gantry). Game Balance to judge the asymmetry with tools/balance.
conflicts.residual: Accepting the asymmetry, or asking for a symmetric mechanic, is the owner's decision.

conflicts.conflict: Protection applies, but a blocked attack is something the attacker sees fail. An attacker who knows they still had their opportunity learns that the victim is Protected, which "does not automatically authorize Protection disclosure".
conflicts.solution: The design discloses as little as the rules allow: one STOPPED for Protection and for a spent opportunity alike, with no reason on either phone; the victim cannot tell which it was; no one else learns anything. The attacker's inference cannot be removed without a third reason for a stop, which the rules do not have.
conflicts.residual: The owner confirms that the attacker's inference is acceptable, or chooses a different block.

conflicts.conflict: With two participants, a death on the Task names the killer to anyone who knows who went: the return shows the body, and the other participant is the only possible cause. The rules forbid automatic attribution but make it deducible.
conflicts.solution: No phone states a killer, a cause or a Task death; the death is shown as any death. The owner has decided that other players can see on the board who is away (11 November 2026), so after a death everyone can work out the survivor; that is accepted, and nothing states it. Accidents (the owner's decision, the same day) make any Task death possibly an accident, so the survivor always has a story.
conflicts.residual: Settled by the owner's decision: nothing left to decide.

openItems.item: Whether one dose is one package. PROPOSED: yes.

When a Volunteer's initiation is spent. PROPOSED: when a Partner joins and the Task starts (a decline or a withdrawn request does not spend it); a Task cancelled by the Partner's disconnect gives it back, one cancelled by the Volunteer's own does not.
Whether a deliberate disconnect costs anything (conflict 1).

Who can be asked as a Partner (PROPOSED: a living player outside the Hospital and the Jail, not on a Task), how long they have to answer (PROPOSED: 15 s, and no answer is a decline), and whether a Volunteer may ask the same player again after a decline (PROPOSED: not for this start). That a Partner can decline is the owner's decision.
Who runs which control. PROPOSED: the server at random (conflict 2).
Whether other players learn the result. PROPOSED: only as the food stock shows it, delivered (+5) or not. That they can see who is away is the owner's decision.
When a Task may start (which phases count as outside ordinary turns), and whether two Tasks may run at once.
The PROPOSED timing: 4 s briefing, 45 s deadline, 8 s grace, 300 ms between presses.
The survivor asymmetry (conflict 2) and the food economy: five packages, five per delivery, one dose per player at each Eating step.
The Eating step's place in the round and its order: with the stock short, the order decides who goes to the Hospital.

PROPOSED: attacks are deliberate. A press made on an older picture, or a hold's repeat, never attacks; with the partner moving at the same moment it counts toward an accident instead (TASK_MOVE shown and repeat).
The accident numbers: a 1 in 4 chance, a half-second window, and the two zones (PROPOSED).
Whether Protection saves a participant from an accident. PROPOSED: yes, as a close call, which reveals nothing.
TASK_MOVE and the Task projection in packages/contracts/, and the ruleset version that adopts this Task.
The Engine Task is not designed here.
